newsitem.title: USA: Ivax, Bergen Brunswig merger off.
newsitem.headline: Ivax, Bergen Brunswig merger off.

text.p: Bergen Brunswig Corp said on Thursday it had terminated a previously announced $1.6 billion merger agreement with IVAX Corp and planned to file a lawsuit against IVAX alleging breach of the merger pact.
Ivax said in a separate statement Bergen terminated the merger without good cause.
Drug wholesaler Bergen said in November it had agreed to buy generic drug maker IVAX in a deal which would form the United States' first integrated manufacturer and distributor of pharmaceuticals.
Bergen said that while it was terminating its agreement with IVAX, it would continue to pursue a strategy aimed at managing supply channel costs.

"Notwithstanding the termination of the IVAX agreement, we will continue to pursue our strategy, recognizing the valuable role that generics play," Donald Roden, Bergen's president and chief executive officer, said.
Bergen later told Reuters it could not comment on precisely how the merger agreement had been breached because the matter was going into litigation.

"It involves things that have been occurring over the past few months," a company spokewoman said. She said Bergen decided to take action on Thursday but declined to comment further on the nature of the lawsuit.
IVAX said it was prepared to proceed independently.

IVAX Chairman Phillip Frost said: "Recognizing the possibility that the Bergen merger might not be approved or completed, we developed, together with our advisors, a number of contingency strategies geared towards the success of an independent IVAX, and look forward to announcing and implementing those strategies in the near term."
An IVAX spokesman told Reuters the company could not comment or speculate about Bergen's allegations because it had not yet been served with the complaint.
"We don't see any sound basis for their unilateral termination," he said.
The spokesman said IVAX had already fashioned contingency strategies, which it would announce shortly, but he declined to reveal the specifics of those strategies.
